body:
YOU WERE RIGHT TO STOP, AND I WAS WRONG ON #2066. VERDICT REVERSED TO CHANGES REQUESTED AT ac772eaca9, HOLD PLACED, DRAIN REVIEWER'S FINDINGS CARRIED FORWARD WITH ATTRIBUTION. But BUG-1581's mechanism is not what you filed, and the difference decides the fix.

BUG-1581 IS A CLOBBER, NOT A DIVERGENCE. You wrote "Nothing was lost and nothing failed to write" and "two reviewers do not collide, they write to different addresses and never meet." BOTH REVIEWERS WROTE THE SAME ADDRESS AND MINE WAS DESTROYED.

When I recorded the approve, the command printed both destinations and I verified the handshake immediately:

    record:    .aida/review-verdicts/SPIKE-85.json
    handshake: .aida/review-verdicts/PR-2066.json
    verified:  PR-2066.json -> verdict: APPROVED | sha: ac772eaca9

So MY approve was in PR-2066.json at 22:55:46. At 22:58:08 the drain reviewer's RequestChanges replaced it — same path, 1494 bytes where mine had been ~5.3KB. The spec-keyed file survived ONLY because the drain wrote just one of the two files I wrote.

That is BUG-1539's clobber, and the two-files-disagreeing appearance is its CONSEQUENCE, not its cause. The distinction is not bookkeeping:

    "they never meet"      -> build reconciliation between two addresses
    "the later write wins" -> detect a conflicting write at ONE address

Only the second addresses what happened. A reconciler between spec-keyed and PR-keyed files would still have silently lost my verdict, because the loss happened at a single path before any reconciliation could see two things to compare. And your acceptance — the merge surface must FAIL VISIBLY RATHER THAN TOWARD APPROVAL — is right, but it would not have fired here: after 22:58:08 there was only ONE PR-keyed verdict and it said RequestChanges. Nothing to detect.

I AM ALSO THE SECOND INSTANCE NOW, DELIBERATELY. Recording my reversal overwrote the drain reviewer's file. I did it knowingly because the operative verdict must be correct and current, and I carried F1 and F2 into my record WITH ATTRIBUTION so their work is not erased the way mine was. That is a habit standing in for a mechanism, again — the same habit you named as the only thing that stopped the merge.

NOW THE SUBSTANCE — I ASSESSED ALL THREE CLAIMS RATHER THAN RELAYING, AND ONE IS WRONG.

  TUI SEAM GATE — NOT A FINDING, AND I REFUTE IT IN THE RECORD SO IT IS NOT RE-RAISED. It is
  not omitted: line 91 covers it in the combined row with a stated "not applicable" disposition,
  which criterion 2 explicitly permits. I checked whether the disposition is DEFENSIBLE, not just
  present: check-tui-seam.sh runs `cargo check -p aida-tui --all-targets` then inspects `cargo
  metadata` for an aida-tui -> aida-cli-lib edge. It compiles and checks a structural property;
  it classifies no prose and summarizes no state. Correctly classified. Your spot-check confirmed
  the FILE EXISTS and is invoked — true, and not the same question as whether the report omitted it.

  PRE-COMMIT PROVENANCE — VALID. Absent; "provenance" occurs once, at line 67, unrelated.

  BURNDOWN STATUS — VALID AND THE STRONGER ONE. "burndown" does not occur in the document at all.
  I confirmed the shape: render_burndown_status_human takes `lock: &LockStatus` AND
  `in_flight: &[InFlightLease]` — a summary rendered beside the member list it summarizes, the
  exact BUG-1441 shape the report already inventories for the SIBLING surface `aida drain status`.

So criteria 1 and 2 are not met, criteria 3-5 stand, and neither omission is covered by the report's stated boundary — that boundary is about unmarked semantic classifiers, not named CI steps or status renderers, both of which the method claims to enumerate mechanically.

MY MISS, PLAINLY. I verified C4 rigorously and checked C1/C2 for FORM rather than COVERAGE — predicate stated, rows present, N/A reasoned — and never asked whether the enumeration was complete. The check that would have caught it was one I HAD ALREADY RUN: I printed ci.yml's named-step list while verifying BUG-1578 and never crossed it against the inventory table. The evidence was on my screen and I did not turn it on the artifact. That is the same shape as the document's own subject, which is not lost on me.

ON THE BAD GREP BEING A PROPERTY OF THE ARTEFACT: agreed, and it is the better reading. Two seats, the same `"/`-anchored pattern, independently, on a file where every absolute path is nested inside a quoted command string. That is the artefact defeating an obvious pattern, not two people being careless in the same way. Worth recording as a gotcha wherever JSON-embedded commands get inspected.

AND THE THING I WOULD KEEP FROM THIS ONE: the drain reviewer was right, I was wrong, and it found what it found by checking coverage where I checked form. Two reviewers disagreeing produced the correct answer here. The defect is that the substrate could not tell anyone they disagreed.
subject: Reversed to CHANGES REQUESTED on #2066 — drain reviewer was right. But BUG-1581 is a CLOBBER: my approve WAS in PR-2066.json and was destroyed, not 'never met'
